description: Sealed held-out suite: TOON and MStream. Never mined for training data; report scores only in aggregate.

tasks.title: Reorder report rounded up to whole packs
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `stock_levels.json` is provided in the working directory, shaped `{"warehouse": Text, "items": [{"sku": Text, "on_hand": Int, "reorder_at": Int, "pack": Int}, ...]}`. Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `TOON unavailable` and stop. Otherwise print `warehouse <warehouse>`. Then, for each item in file order: an item is fine when `on_hand` is at least `reorder_at`; otherwise it must be reordered in whole packs, using the smallest number of packs of size `pack` that brings `on_hand` up to at least `reorder_at`. For each item that needs reordering print `ORDER <sku> <packs> x <pack> = <units>` where `<units>` is packs times pack; if that item's `on_hand` is 0, append ` (out of stock)` to its line. Print nothing for fine items. After the items print `ok: <number of fine items>`, `to order: <number of ORDER lines>`, and `units: <sum of all units ordered>`, each on its own line. Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
warehouse north-2
ORDER NUT-6 2 x 25 = 50
ORDER WASH-4 1 x 100 = 100 (out of stock)
ORDER CLIP-9 2 x 12 = 24
ok: 2
to order: 3
units: 174

tasks.title: Effective service settings from nested config with defaults
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that parses this JSON service configuration, given as a string literal in the program:

`{"service":{"name":"ledger","http":{"port":8443,"tls":true},"workers":6},"limits":{"rps":250},"log":{"format":"json"}}`

Print the effective value of ten settings, one per line, in this order and exactly in the form `<setting> = <value>`, using the stated default whenever the setting is absent (any missing level of nesting counts as absent):
- `name` from `service` -> `name`, default `unnamed`
- `port` from `service` -> `http` -> `port`, default `80`
- `tls` from `service` -> `http` -> `tls`, default `false`
- `workers` from `service` -> `workers`, default `1`
- `timeout_ms` from `service` -> `http` -> `timeout_ms`, default `30000`
- `rps` from `limits` -> `rps`, default `100`
- `burst` from `limits` -> `burst`, default twice the effective `rps`
- `log.level` from `log` -> `level`, default `info`
- `log.format` from `log` -> `format`, default `text`
- `admin` from `service` -> `admin` -> `enabled`, default `false`

Booleans print as `true`/`false`. Then print `defaults used = <how many of the ten settings fell back to their default>` and finally `url = <scheme>://<name>:<port>` where `<scheme>` is `https` when the effective `tls` is true and `http` otherwise. Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
name = ledger
port = 8443
tls = true
workers = 6
timeout_ms = 30000
rps = 250
burst = 500
log.level = info
log.format = json
admin = false
defaults used = 4
url = https://ledger:8443

tasks.title: Classify mixed-type cells of a JSON row
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that parses this JSON array (one exported spreadsheet row), given as a string literal in the program:

`[42, "n/a", 3.5, true, null, -7, "12", 0.25, false, {"ref": "B2"}, [1, 2, 3], ""]`

For each cell in order print one line `cell <i>: <description>` (zero-based `<i>`) where the description depends on the JSON type of the cell:
- integer: `int <value>`
- number with a fractional part (written with a decimal point): `real <value>` with exactly two decimals
- string: `text "<value>"` (the value wrapped in double quotes; a string that looks like a number is still a string)
- boolean: `bool true` or `bool false`
- null: `empty`
- array: `array of <element count>`
- object: `object`

Then print, each on its own line: `numeric sum = <sum of all integer and real cells>` with exactly two decimals, `texts = <number of string cells>`, `true flags = <number of cells that are the boolean true>`, and `blank = <number of null cells plus empty-string cells>`. Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
cell 0: int 42
cell 1: text "n/a"
cell 2: real 3.50
cell 3: bool true
cell 4: empty
cell 5: int -7
cell 6: text "12"
cell 7: real 0.25
cell 8: bool false
cell 9: object
cell 10: array of 3
cell 11: text ""
numeric sum = 38.75
texts = 3
true flags = 1
blank = 2

tasks.title: Group orders by region with paid, refunded and net totals
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `orders.json` is provided in the working directory. Its top level is an array of orders shaped `[{"id": Text, "region": Text, "status": Text, "total": Int}, ...]` where `status` is `paid`, `refunded` or `pending`. Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `cannot parse orders` and stop. Otherwise group the orders by `region`, keeping regions in the order they first appear in the file (do not assume which regions exist). For each region print `<region>: n=<number of orders>, paid <sum of paid totals>, refunded <sum of refunded totals>, net <paid minus refunded>`; pending orders count toward `n` but toward neither sum. Then print `best region = <region> (<net>)` for the region with the highest net (the earliest region on a tie), `pending = <ids of pending orders in file order, joined with commas>` (or `pending = none` if there are none), and `grand net = <sum of all region nets>`. Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
west: n=3, paid 215, refunded 40, net 175
east: n=3, paid 205, refunded 0, net 205
south: n=2, paid 210, refunded 210, net 0
best region = east (205)
pending = o-105
grand net = 380

tasks.title: Rank students by mean score with stable ties
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that parses this JSON gradebook, given as a string literal in the program:

`{"course":"chem-2","students":[{"name":"Ines","scores":[78,85,90]},{"name":"Bo","scores":[92,88]},{"name":"Cato","scores":[]},{"name":"Dara","scores":[85,90,78]},{"name":"Eli"},{"name":"Fay","scores":[100,61,70,95]}]}`

Each student's mean is the average of their `scores`. A student whose `scores` array is empty or missing has no mean and is not ranked. Print `course <course>`, then the ranked students from highest mean to lowest, one per line as `#<rank> <name> <mean> (<count> scores)` with rank starting at 1 and the mean printed with exactly two decimals; students with equal means keep their input order. Then print `no scores: <names of unranked students in input order, joined with ", ">`, `class average = <mean of every individual score of every student>` with exactly two decimals, and `best single score = <highest individual score> (<name of the student who has it>)` (the first such student in input order on a tie). Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
course chem-2
#1 Bo 90.00 (2 scores)
#2 Ines 84.33 (3 scores)
#3 Dara 84.33 (3 scores)
#4 Fay 81.50 (4 scores)
no scores: Cato, Eli
class average = 84.33
best single score = 100 (Fay)

tasks.title: Contact audit distinguishing absent object, absent key and blank value
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `members.json` is provided in the working directory, shaped `{"members": [{"id": Int, "name": Text, "contact": {"email": Text, "phone": Text}, "active": Bool}, ...]}`, where `name`, `contact`, `active`, and each of the two keys inside `contact` may be missing. Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `member audit skipped: no TOON support` and stop. Otherwise print one line per member in file order: `#<id> <name>: <status>`, using `(no name)` when `name` is missing. `<status>` is `no contact` when there is no `contact` object, `no email` when `contact` exists but has no `email` key, `email blank` when `email` is present but the empty string, and `email <address>` otherwise. A member whose `active` is false gets ` [inactive]` appended to the line; a missing `active` means active. After the members print, each on its own line: `reachable by email = <members with a non-empty email>`, `reachable by phone = <members with a non-empty phone>`, `unreachable = <members with neither>`, and `mailing list = <non-empty emails of active members in file order, joined with ;>`. Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
#7 Rosa: email rosa@mail.test
#8 Tomas: no email
#9 (no name): email anon9@mail.test
#10 Wen: no contact
#11 Yusuf: email blank [inactive]
reachable by email = 2
reachable by phone = 3
unreachable = 1
mailing list = rosa@mail.test;anon9@mail.test

tasks.title: Validate a meter series of mixed JSON values
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that parses this JSON meter dump, given as a string literal in the program:

`{"meter":"pump-7","unit":"pulses","samples":[120, 135, null, 98, "ERR", 142, 101.5, true, 111]}`

Only whole-number (integer) entries of `samples` are valid readings. A number with a fractional part is rejected as fractional; any other value (null, string, boolean, ...) is rejected as junk. Positions are zero-based indexes into `samples`. Print exactly these lines:
`meter <meter> (<unit>)`
`valid = <number of valid readings>`
`fractional = <count> at <positions joined with commas>`
`junk = <count> at <positions joined with commas>`
`mean = <mean of the valid readings, exactly two decimals>`
`min = <smallest valid reading> at <its position>`
`max = <largest valid reading> at <its position>`
`range = <max minus min>`
`above mean = <number of valid readings strictly greater than the mean>`
Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
meter pump-7 (pulses)
valid = 5
fractional = 1 at 6
junk = 3 at 2,4,7
mean = 121.20
min = 98 at 3
max = 142 at 5
range = 44
above mean = 2

tasks.title: Cluster inventory over partially specified nested node specs
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `cluster.json` is provided in the working directory, shaped `{"cluster": {"name": Text, "nodes": [{"host": Text, "spec": {"cpu": Int, "mem": {"gb": Int}}, "tags": [Text, ...]}, ...]}}`. Any node may lack `spec`, `spec` may lack `cpu` or `mem`, and `tags` may be missing or empty. Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `no structured data support` and stop. Otherwise print one line per node in file order: `<host>: cpu <cpu>, mem <gb>G, tags <tags>`, where an unknown cpu prints as `cpu ?`, an unknown memory size prints as `mem ?` (no `G`), and `<tags>` is the tags joined with `|`, or `-` when there are none. Then print `cluster <name>: <node count> nodes, <sum of known cpu> cpu, <sum of known gb>G`, `gpu nodes = <hosts tagged gpu, in file order, joined with commas>`, `incomplete = <nodes missing cpu or memory>`, and `largest memory = <host with the most memory>` (the first on a tie). Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
bx-01: cpu 16, mem 64G, tags gpu|ssd
bx-02: cpu 8, mem ?, tags ssd
bx-03: cpu ?, mem 128G, tags -
bx-04: cpu ?, mem ?, tags gpu|spot|ssd
bx-05: cpu 32, mem 256G, tags -
cluster batch-east: 5 nodes, 56 cpu, 448G
gpu nodes = bx-01,bx-04

tasks.title: Monthly spend grouped by date prefix
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `spend report unavailable` and stop. Otherwise parse this JSON array of expenses, given as a string literal in the program:

`[{"date":"2026-01-04","cat":"food","amt":12.40},{"date":"2026-01-19","cat":"travel","amt":88.00},{"date":"2026-02-02","cat":"food","amt":9.95},{"date":"2026-01-27","cat":"food","amt":15.10},{"date":"2026-03-11","cat":"rent","amt":700.00},{"date":"2026-02-14","cat":"gift","amt":45.50},{"date":"2026-03-30","cat":"food","amt":21.05}]`

Group the expenses by month, the first seven characters of `date` (`YYYY-MM`), keeping months in the order they first appear (entries of one month are not necessarily adjacent). For each month print `<month>: <count> entries, <sum of amt>`. Then print `food share = <sum of amt for cat food> of <sum of all amt>` and `largest = <date> <cat> <amt>` for the single largest expense (the first on a tie). Every amount is printed with exactly two decimals. Release the parsed document before returning.

tasks.title: Percent-encode a query string into a memory stream byte by byte
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that percent-encodes the query string `q=red shoes&max=40%&path=a/b c`, given as a string literal in the program. Letters `A`-`Z` and `a`-`z`, digits, the four characters `-` `_` `.` `~`, and the separators `=` and `&` are copied unchanged; every other character is replaced by `%` followed by its character code as two uppercase hexadecimal digits (a space becomes `%20`). Build the encoded result in an in-memory byte stream, appending exactly one byte at a time, then read the stream's whole contents back as text and free the stream. Print, each on its own line: `input = <input>`, `encoded = <text read back from the stream>`, `escaped = <number of characters that were replaced>`, and `bytes = <length of the encoded text>`.
tasks.expected_stdout:
input = q=red shoes&max=40%&path=a/b c
encoded = q=red%20shoes&max=40%25&path=a%2Fb%20c
escaped = 4
bytes = 38

tasks.title: Memory stream save to file and load back
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that creates an in-memory byte stream initialised from the text `alpha,3
beta,12
gamma,7
` (three lines, each ending in a newline), then appends the line `delta,5` plus a trailing newline to that stream one byte at a time. Save the stream to the file `snapshot.txt` and free it. tasks.title: Parse a JSON body held in a memory stream
tasks.prompt: A file named `response.json` holding a saved API response is provided in the working directory, shaped `{"status": Text, "page": {"number": Int, "size": Int}, "results": [{"id": Int, "title": Text, "votes": Int, "labels": [Text, ...]}, ...]}`; `labels` may be missing. Write an Aether program that first checks `has_toon()`; if structured-data support is missing, print `json support missing` and stop. Otherwise treat the file like an HTTP response body: load it into an in-memory byte stream, take the stream's contents as text, free the stream, and parse that text as JSON. Print `body bytes = <length of the text>`. If `status` is not `ok`, print `request failed: <status>` and stop. Otherwise print `status = ok, page <page number> of size <page size>`, then one line per result in order as `<id> <title> (<votes>) <labels>` where `<labels>` is the labels joined with commas or `-` when there are none. Finally print `bugs = <number of results labelled bug>` and `top = <title of the result with the most votes>` (the first on a tie). Release the parsed document before returning.
tasks.expected_stdout:
body bytes = 330
status = ok, page 2 of size 4
31 Fix login (12) bug,auth
32 Dark theme (40) ui
33 Crash on save (27) bug
34 Docs typo (3) -
bugs = 2
top = Dark theme
